sectors.name: Silicon
sectors.blurb: Who designs the chips, who makes them, who supplies the memory and who sells the machines that print them.

positions.name: AI accelerators
positions.metric: Nvidia Data Center revenue of $89.0bn in the quarter to 26 Jul 2026, up 117% year on year. Estimates of Nvidia's share of AI accelerator revenue run from about 70% to over 80%, depending on whether in-house chips are counted.

players.stat: Data Center $89.0bn, quarter to 26 Jul 2026. Total revenue $96.2bn. Q3 guide $108bn.
players.why: Sells the chips, the networking and the software together, so a customer buys one working rack.
players.cond: Large buyers shift volume to in-house chips, and China, where IDC has Nvidia at 34% of H1 2026 shipments.

players.stat: Data Center segment $6.7bn, up 107% year on year, Q2 2026.
players.why: Its Helios racks are deployed by Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle, and two labs have signed multi-gigawatt supply deals.
players.cond: The MI450 class has to ship in volume in the second half of 2026 and the software has to keep pace.

players.stat: 28% of China AI chip shipments in H1 2026 (572,000 units), against Nvidia's 34% (IDC, as reported).
players.why: Its shipments nearly doubled while Nvidia's fell 44% as China steered buyers to domestic chips.
players.cond: Access to enough advanced manufacturing capacity to keep growing.

players.stat: IPO priced at $185 on 13 May 2026, raising $5.55bn. An OpenAI agreement valued above $20bn is cited in its S-1/A (reported).
players.why: Builds one chip from an entire wafer, a different premise from stacking many small chips.
players.cond: Turning the OpenAI commitment into delivered capacity.

players.stat: Non-exclusive licence of its inference technology to Nvidia (Dec 2025), reported at about $20bn. Its founder and team joined Nvidia. Groq continues as a separate company.
players.why: Nvidia paid for low-latency inference technology it did not have.
players.cond: A reported Justice Department review and a Delaware stockholder suit over how the deal was structured.

players.stat: $1.5bn Series E at a $6.2bn valuation, 19 Oct 2026.
players.why: Sells open, modular AI servers to buyers who want an alternative stack.
players.cond: Turning the round into Galaxy server shipments and manufacturing capacity.

players.stat: $500m Series B in January 2026 (CB Insights). Later offers at higher valuations are reported and unconfirmed.
players.why: Bets that one model architecture will dominate, so a chip built only for it wins on cost.
players.cond: Whether transformers stay the dominant architecture.

positions.name: Custom chips for the biggest buyers
positions.metric: Broadcom AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7bn in the quarter to 2 Aug 2026, up 221% year on year. Guide for the next quarter is $21.7bn.

players.stat: AI semiconductor revenue $16.7bn, quarter to 2 Aug 2026. Custom accelerators were 73% of AI revenue (third-party summary).
players.why: Co-designs the accelerators for the biggest buyers and sells the Ethernet that connects them.
players.cond: Customers bring more design in-house, or OpenAI's chips arrive late. Racks are planned from the second half of 2026.

players.stat: Anthropic can use up to 1 million TPUs. Meta is reported to have agreed a multibillion-dollar TPU deal (Feb 2026).
players.why: Sells its own chip capacity to rivals in AI, which gives the chip volume no single product could.
players.cond: Anthropic said it will keep using Amazon's Trainium and Nvidia GPUs too.

players.stat: Anthropic's primary training partner (reported).
players.why: Trainium gives AWS a cost advantage and a reason for AI labs to build on its cloud.
players.cond: Labs spreading workloads across several chip families.

players.stat: Broadcom and Marvell are estimated to control about 95% of custom accelerator co-design (secondary estimate).
players.why: The only other scaled partner a buyer can call.
players.cond: Winning a flagship program the way Broadcom won Google's.

players.stat: 10 gigawatts of OpenAI-designed accelerators with Broadcom, under a signed term sheet. Racks planned from the second half of 2026 to the end of 2029.
players.why: A model lab that designs its own chips can tune the hardware to its models.
players.cond: First silicon has to ship on schedule. Terms were not disclosed.

positions.name: CPUs and architecture
positions.metric: x86 unit share, Q2 2026 (Mercury Research, as reported): Intel 69.3%, AMD 30.7%. Intel fell below 70% for the first time since 1995.

players.stat: Q2 2026 revenue $16.1bn, up 25%. Data Center and AI $6.3bn, up 59%. x86 share 69.3%.
players.why: Still ships about seven in ten x86 chips, and Nvidia bought $5bn of its stock and will co-develop x86 products with it.
players.cond: AMD keeps taking share, and 14A needs a named outside anchor customer.

players.stat: x86 share 30.7%, or 34.1% with semi-custom and embedded. Server share reported near 34.5%, and it varies by definition.
players.why: Has taken share in every segment as Intel's supply and entry-level lineup stumbled.
players.cond: Intel's supply recovering.

players.stat: Q1 FY27 revenue $1.29bn, up 22%. Royalties $715m. Data center royalties more than doubling. Demand for its own AGI CPU above $2bn for FY27 to FY28 (company).
players.why: Collects a royalty on most chips outside PCs, and now sells silicon of its own.
players.cond: Licensees object when the licensor competes with them, and RISC-V offers a way out.

players.stat: Won its Nuvia licence case against Arm (Sept 2025), which Arm said it would appeal. Agreed to buy Alphawave for about $2.4bn to enter data center.
players.why: Holds a licence it has now defended in court, and is buying connectivity IP.
players.cond: The appeal, and winning a data center customer.

positions.name: Foundries
positions.metric: Share of top-ten foundry revenue, 2Q26 (TrendForce): TSMC 72.5%, Samsung 5.9%, SMIC 5.4%, UMC 3.9%, GlobalFoundries 3.2%. Top ten together: $53.49bn.

players.stat: 72.5% share, 2Q26, on about $40.2bn of revenue, up 12.1% on the quarter.
players.why: Makes the leading-edge chips for Nvidia, Apple and most others.
players.cond: Taiwan concentration, and whether Samsung or Intel win 2nm customers.

players.stat: 5.9% share in 2Q26, down from 6.5%. A $16.5bn Tesla AI6 contract at Taylor, Texas, runs to 2033 (reported).
players.why: Has an anchor customer for its US fab.
players.cond: 2nm yields and more named customers.

players.stat: 5.4% share in 2Q26, up from 5.1%. Revenue above $3bn, up about 20% on the quarter.
players.why: China steering domestic buyers to domestic chips.
players.cond: Equipment access under export controls.

players.stat: External revenue $293m and an operating loss of $2.1bn in Q2 2026. 14A volume ramp set for 2028. Tesla is reported as a 14A customer, unconfirmed.
players.why: The only Western leading-edge alternative to TSMC, with state and investor backing.
players.cond: Customers decide on 14A between the second half of 2026 and the first half of 2027.

players.stat: UMC 3.9% and GlobalFoundries 3.2% in 2Q26.
players.why: Mature-node capacity for cars, industry and communications.
players.cond: Chinese mature-node capacity and pricing.

players.stat: About 267.6bn yen raised in Feb 2026, plus 150bn yen from Japan's METI in June 2026. 2nm mass production targeted for 2027.
players.why: A state-backed attempt to build a leading-edge Japanese foundry from scratch.
players.cond: Reaching working yields and signing paying customers.

positions.name: Memory
positions.metric: DRAM share, Q2 2026 (Counterpoint): Samsung 38%, SK hynix 25 to 26%, Micron 24 to 25%, CXMT about 10%. HBM: SK hynix about 50%, Samsung about 33%, Micron about 18%.

players.stat: Retook the DRAM lead in Q2 2026 with 38 to 39%. HBM share about 33%, rising.
players.why: Scale across DRAM and the HBM4 generation now shipping.
players.cond: Counterpoint and IDC rank the leaders differently, so the lead is contested.

players.stat: HBM share about 50% in Q2 2026, down from 64% a year earlier. DRAM 25 to 26%. IDC had it first in 2025 DRAM at 34.8%.
players.why: Built the HBM that sits next to Nvidia's chips and still leads it.
players.cond: Samsung's HBM4 ramp. It priced a Nasdaq ADR offering of about $26.5bn in July 2026 (reported).

players.stat: DRAM 24 to 25% and HBM about 18% in Q2 2026.
players.why: The one scaled US memory maker.
players.cond: Holding HBM share as Samsung ramps.

players.stat: About 10% of DRAM in Q2 2026 (Counterpoint).
players.why: Chinese buyers favoring domestic supply.
players.cond: Export controls on equipment, and moving up to HBM.

positions.name: Chip equipment
positions.metric: ASML net sales of EUR 9.3bn in Q2 2026. Full-year 2026 guide EUR 43 to 45bn, with about 65 low-NA EUV systems to ship. ASML, Applied Materials, Lam, Tokyo Electron and KLA were the top five in 2025 (TechInsights).

players.stat: Net sales EUR 9.3bn in Q2 2026, with EUR 3.8bn from EUV systems.
players.why: The only company that makes EUV machines, so every leading-edge fab is its customer.
players.cond: China's share of its sales (about 14% in Q2 by one estimate), and a rival lithography method.

players.stat: Second-largest IC equipment supplier in 2025 (TechInsights).
players.why: Broadest set of deposition and etch tools.
players.cond: Export controls on China sales.

players.stat: Third in 2025 (TechInsights).
players.why: Strong in etch and in memory, which is booming.
players.cond: Memory capex cycles.

players.stat: Fourth in 2025 (TechInsights).
players.why: Leads in coating and developing tools.
players.cond: Japan and China export policy.

players.stat: Fifth in 2025 (TechInsights).
players.why: Inspection and process control grows with chip complexity.
players.cond: China exposure.

players.stat: 2025 revenue forecast of 46.8 to 52.0bn yuan (Jan 2026 forecast, secondary source).
players.why: Chinese fabs buying domestic tools.
players.cond: Margins under price pressure from domestic rivals.

players.stat: 2025 revenue 12.4bn yuan, up 36.6%. Gross margin fell 1.9 points to 39.2%.
players.why: Chinese fabs buying domestic etch tools.
players.cond: Pricing pressure among Chinese equipment vendors, which a Needham analyst said is starting to cut into margins.

players.stat: $100m Series A at a valuation above $1bn, Oct 2025. Targets production in 2028. Claims unproven at scale.
players.why: Replaces the light source of lithography with a compact particle accelerator that writes patterns with X-rays.
players.cond: A working tool at commercial scale. It has no revenue and the founders have no prior chip background.

sectors.name: Infrastructure and data centers
sectors.blurb: The networks, storage, servers, buildings, money and power that turn chips into AI capacity.

positions.name: Networking
positions.metric: Ethernet is about two-thirds of AI cluster switch sales (Q1 2026), up from under 20% in late 2023. Celestica and Nvidia led 2025 with a combined 50% share. In 2Q26 Celestica led Ethernet AI back-end switch sales, Nvidia was close behind, Arista third and Cisco fourth and gaining the most share (Dell'Oro).

players.stat: Led Ethernet AI back-end switch sales in 2Q26 (Dell'Oro).
players.why: Builds switches to the specification of the largest cloud buyers.
players.cond: Buyers moving design in-house or to branded vendors.

players.stat: Close second in Ethernet AI back-end switches, 2Q26. InfiniBand sales more than tripled in Q1 2026 (Dell'Oro).
players.why: Sells InfiniBand and Ethernet together with its GPUs, so the network is part of the rack.
players.cond: Ethernet's rising share.

players.stat: Q2 2026 revenue $3.04bn, up 37.7%. 2026 outlook about $12.6bn. Targets at least $3.5bn of AI fabric revenue.
players.why: Won the cloud switch market that AI buyers extended.
players.cond: Deferred AI revenue timing, and Cisco and Celestica competing for the same orders.

players.stat: AI networking revenue up more than 2.5 times year on year in the quarter to 2 Aug 2026 (third-party summary).
players.why: Its switch silicon sits inside many of the boxes above.
players.cond: Nvidia pushing its own Ethernet silicon.

players.stat: Hyperscale AI orders of $9.3bn in fiscal 2026, about 4.5 times the year before. Expects $7.5bn of hyperscaler AI revenue in fiscal 2027.
players.why: Ranked fourth in 2Q26 and gained the most share (Dell'Oro).
players.cond: Converting orders into shipments.

players.stat: Reported to have completed a roughly $3.25bn purchase of Celestial AI, a photonic fabric startup (single secondary source).
players.why: Buying light-based interconnect to extend its data center position.
players.cond: Integrating and shipping the technology.

players.stat: Series E reported at $500m in March 2026 at about $3.75bn to $3.8bn. Sources conflict.
players.why: Replaces copper links between chips with light.
players.cond: Volume production and a major customer.

positions.name: Storage
positions.metric: No audited share figure exists for AI storage. VAST Data raised $1bn at a $30bn valuation in April 2026 (reported). DDN took $300m at $5bn in January 2025 (Blackstone). Pure Storage, now Everpure, reported $3.7bn of fiscal 2026 revenue.

players.stat: Launched its Lightning parallel file system in April 2026, positioned against DDN, VAST and WEKA (reported).
players.why: Already sells the servers, so storage sells with them.
players.cond: Specialists keeping a performance lead.

players.stat: Fiscal 2025 revenue $6.65bn (reported).
players.why: Large installed base in enterprise data.
players.cond: Whether AI workloads buy from the installed base or from specialists.

players.stat: Fiscal 2026 revenue $3.7bn (reported). Invested in Wasabi's January 2026 round.
players.why: All-flash systems sell into AI data pipelines.
players.cond: Price of flash as memory costs rise.

players.stat: $1bn raised at $30bn, 22 Apr 2026. Reports over $500m of committed recurring revenue and positive cash flow, both company-reported.
players.why: Fastest-growing independent, with Nvidia reported as a backer.
players.cond: Staying ahead of Dell and Nvidia's own storage push.

players.stat: $300m from Blackstone at a $5bn valuation, January 2025. BofA Securities was its exclusive adviser.
players.why: Runs inside the largest clusters, including xAI's Colossus by its own account.
players.cond: Reaching the roughly $1bn revenue projected for 2026.

players.stat: Valued above $1.6bn in an older report. Says it works with 12 of the Fortune 50.
players.why: Parallel file system built for GPU clusters.
players.cond: Competing with better-funded rivals.

positions.name: Servers and systems
positions.metric: Server revenue share, Q1 2026 (IDC): Dell 16.5% on $20.28bn, Super Micro 7.6%, Lenovo 4.6%, IEIT 3.3%, HPE 3%. Unbranded ODM direct supply, where Foxconn, Quanta and Wistron sit, was 50.2% of revenue.

players.stat: Fiscal 2026: $64bn of AI server orders, $25bn shipped, $43bn backlog. Q1 FY27 AI server revenue $16.1bn and orders $24.4bn (reported).
players.why: Largest branded vendor with enterprise reach.
players.cond: Component supply. IDC says DRAM, flash, CPUs and drives limit shipments.

players.stat: Unbranded ODM direct supply was 50.2% of server revenue in Q1 2026 (IDC). The tracker does not split it by company.
players.why: Build to the buyer's design at the lowest cost.
players.cond: Margins, and buyers designing their own racks.

players.stat: 7.6% share in Q1 2026 (IDC).
players.why: Fast to ship new GPU systems.
players.cond: Margins and governance questions at smaller scale.

players.stat: 4.6% share in Q1 2026 (IDC).
players.why: Global reach.
players.cond: China exposure.

players.stat: 3% share in Q1 2026 (IDC).
players.why: Large enterprise and supercomputing base.
players.cond: Share loss to Dell and ODMs.

positions.name: Data center landlords and financiers
positions.metric: Equinix Q2 2026 revenue of $2.63bn and record annualized bookings of $424m, up 23%. Digital Realty reported a record $1.9bn backlog (100% share). Blackstone projects 7 GW of data center leasing across its platforms in 2026.

players.stat: Q2 2026 revenue $2.63bn. Presales up more than 50%. Stabilized sites about 82% utilized.
players.why: Sells interconnection as well as space, so customers connect to one another there.
players.cond: Hyperscalers building their own campuses.

players.stat: Record backlog of $1.9bn and two further hyperscale US leases worth $410m of annual rent after Q2 2026.
players.why: Large wholesale footprint with long leases.
players.cond: Power availability for new sites.

players.stat: Blackstone says QTS's leased capacity is 15 times what it was five years ago. Other sources cite 3 GW commissioned and over 5 GW contracted.
players.why: Owned by a firm that finances the build and the power too.
players.cond: Different capacity measures give different sizes.

players.stat: Holds 80% of the Hyperion joint venture with Meta, funded by about $27bn of development cost.
players.why: Supplies off-balance-sheet capital that lets a platform build faster.
players.cond: The A+ rated $27.3bn bond reportedly traded down to 94.4 cents (single source).

players.stat: A $35bn package to buy chips for lease to Anthropic is reported as the largest private credit deal on record.
players.why: Finances the chips as well as the buildings.
players.cond: Credit performance if AI demand slows.

players.stat: Series F of $3.9bn at about $30.9bn post-money reported for Sept 2026.
players.why: Builds campuses around cheap power and rents GPUs from them.
players.cond: Filling capacity at those prices.

positions.name: Power and cooling
positions.metric: GE Vernova's backlog stood at $176bn at the end of Q2 2026, with gas turbine slot reservations at 56 GW. Vertiv's trailing orders grew 81% organically. Bloom Energy's backlog was reported near $6bn, up 140%.

players.stat: Backlog $176bn at end of Q2 2026. Gas turbine backlog 44 GW in Q1 2026 and slot reservations 56 GW.
players.why: Turbine slots are booked into 2030, so buyers queue for it.
players.cond: Whether on-site gas becomes the fast route around grid waits.

players.stat: Trailing organic orders up 81%. Q2 2026 sales up 24% (secondary). A year-end 2025 backlog near $15bn is cited and conflicts with another report.
players.why: Sells the power and cooling inside the racks as they get denser.
players.cond: Liquid cooling standards and rivals' share.

players.stat: Data center orders reportedly up about 200% in Q4 2025.
players.why: Electrical gear at every step between grid and rack.
players.cond: Lead times and copper costs.

players.stat: Fuel cell backlog near $6bn, up 140% year on year, at the start of 2026.
players.why: Delivers power on site without waiting for the grid.
players.cond: Cost of gas and scale of deliveries.

players.stat: 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to restart the Crane nuclear plant in 2027 (reported).
players.why: Owns the nuclear plants buyers already trust.
players.cond: Regulatory approvals and the restart date.

players.stat: IPO raised about $1bn in April 2026. Its Amazon deal could reach up to 5 GW of nuclear power by 2039.
players.why: Small modular reactors can sit next to a campus.
players.cond: First plants have not been built yet.

players.stat: A binding Meta prepayment and development funding agreement. First phase targeted for 2030, full capacity by 2034.
players.why: A customer pays up front to get power built.
players.cond: Licensing and construction schedules.

players.stat: Two new Natrium units of up to 690 MW for Meta, announced January 2026.
players.why: A buyer committing years ahead to a reactor design.
players.cond: Construction timeline.

players.stat: Raised $1bn in August 2026 (Bloomberg, as reported).
players.why: Venture money is flowing into reactor developers.
players.cond: Demonstrating a working reactor.

sectors.name: Cloud and compute
sectors.blurb: Who rents out the computers, and who is catching up by renting only the AI ones.

positions.name: Public cloud
positions.metric: Share of cloud infrastructure spending, Q2 2026 (Synergy Research, as reported): Amazon 28%, Microsoft 20%, Google 15%, in a market of about $143bn. Other trackers give different splits.

players.stat: AWS sales $42.2bn in Q2 2026, up 37%, with operating income of $16.6bn. Amazon's net income included $53.4bn of non-operating gains, mainly from its Anthropic investments.
players.why: Largest installed base, and the fastest growth in 18 quarters.
players.cond: Google and Microsoft growing faster from smaller bases.

players.stat: Azure and other cloud services grew 43% in the quarter to June 2026. Microsoft Cloud revenue $59.3bn in the quarter (secondary reports). Commercial backlog reported at $678bn.
players.why: Sells cloud into customers who already run its software, and holds a large OpenAI stake.
players.cond: Capacity to serve the backlog.

players.stat: Google Cloud revenue about $24.8bn in Q2 2026, up 82%, with a reported $514bn backlog (secondary coverage of Alphabet's 22 July report).
players.why: Sells its own TPUs and Gemini alongside the cloud, and gained share in the Synergy data.
players.cond: Whether the backlog converts to revenue. About half is expected within 24 months.

players.stat: Cloud infrastructure revenue $7.4bn in the quarter to August 2026, up 121%. Remaining performance obligations $664bn. Free cash flow was negative $5bn.
players.why: Signed the largest AI contracts and delivered more than 300,000 GPUs since the end of May.
players.cond: Pre-earnings estimates put OpenAI at about half of the backlog (analyst estimate), so one customer carries much of it.

players.stat: AI cloud and compute revenue 48.44bn yuan in the June 2026 quarter, up 45%. Capital spending up 75% to 67.68bn yuan (reported).
players.why: Leads China, where US chips are restricted and domestic ones are rising.
players.cond: Access to enough AI chips, and Huawei and Tencent.

positions.name: GPU clouds and inference platforms
positions.metric: CoreWeave revenue of $2.575bn in Q2 2026, more than double a year earlier, with a revenue backlog of about $104bn at 30 June. 2026 revenue guide $12.4bn to $13.2bn.

players.stat: Q2 2026 revenue $2.575bn. Backlog about $104bn plus more than $25bn added in early Q3. Net interest expense $640m.
players.why: Rents GPUs by the contract to buyers that cannot build fast enough, including Meta, OpenAI and Microsoft.
players.cond: Customer concentration (Microsoft was about 67% of 2025 revenue) and the interest bill.

players.stat: Q2 revenue about $582m. Microsoft agreed to pay up to $17.4bn through 2031. Meta agreed $12bn of dedicated compute over five years, with up to $15bn more.
players.why: Long contracts from the two biggest platform buyers.
players.cond: Funding: it leans on convertible debt and customer prepayments.

players.stat: Series E of more than $1.5bn in November 2025 and a $1bn credit facility in May 2026. TechCrunch reports it plans to raise up to $4bn before a 2027 IPO.
players.why: A GPU cloud with a long record serving researchers.
players.cond: Winning a flagship contract as large as CoreWeave's.

players.stat: $1.505bn Series D at a $17.5bn valuation, July 2026, with annualized revenue reported above $1bn.
players.why: Serves open models fast and cheaply to developers.
players.cond: Frontier labs' models staying closed and pricing falling.

players.stat: $800m Series C at an $8.3bn valuation, 1 July 2026.
players.why: Runs and trains open models for companies that want to own them.
players.cond: Competing with the hyperscalers' own model services.

players.stat: Sources conflict: a $300m round at $5bn in early 2026, or $1.5bn at $13bn in June 2026.
players.why: Deploys customers' own models with the plumbing included.
players.cond: Funding details unverified.

players.stat: Sources conflict: a reported $750m at $15.75bn in October 2026, or an earlier $2.5bn in talks.
players.why: Serverless compute for AI jobs.
players.cond: Funding details unverified.

players.stat: $70m equity round, January 2026, led by L2 Point with Pure Storage and Fidelity, at about $1.8bn.
players.why: Prices storage with no exit fee, which changes what customers are buying.
players.cond: Hyperscalers waived exit fees for customers who leave, which narrows the gap.

sectors.name: AI models and platforms
sectors.blurb: The labs that build the models and the apps that sell them.

positions.name: Frontier labs
positions.metric: Enterprise LLM API spend, late 2025 (Menlo Ventures survey of 495 US decision makers, excluding consumer revenue): Anthropic about 40%, OpenAI 27%, Google 21%. Ramp's August 2026 data shows 43.8% of US businesses paying Anthropic and 39.8% paying OpenAI.

players.stat: Run-rate revenue $65bn at end of July 2026 (CNBC). $65bn Series H at a $965bn post-money valuation in May 2026 (Orrick). Reported to have confidentially filed for an IPO.
players.why: Leads enterprise API spend and coding, and buys compute from Google, Amazon, Nvidia and AMD.
players.cond: Compute supply, and OpenAI and Google closing the enterprise gap.

players.stat: $122bn round at an $852bn post-money valuation, March 2026. Amazon committed $50bn, and Nvidia and SoftBank $30bn each. A further $30bn raise at $1.25tn to $1.4tn is reported in talks, unsigned.
players.why: The largest consumer audience, with signed compute commitments across Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Cerebras and Oracle.
players.cond: Turning compute commitments into revenue. Amazon's $35bn is contingent on an IPO or an AGI milestone.

players.stat: Gemini app at 950 million monthly users on Alphabet's July 2026 call and 1 billion by 11 Aug (reported). AI Mode in Search passed 1 billion monthly users.
players.why: Owns the distribution (Search, Android, Workspace) and its own chips.
players.cond: Turning usage into paid enterprise share, where Menlo put it at 21%.

players.stat: 2026 capital spending guided to $130bn to $145bn. Q2 2026 capex $31.1bn and free cash flow $784m. Meta AI user counts vary from 640 million to 1.5 billion across trackers and none is Meta-confirmed.
players.why: Spends at hyperscaler scale and has 3 billion-plus users to deploy models to.
players.cond: Whether the spending produces a model that leads, since investors sold the shares after Q2.

players.stat: SpaceX bought xAI in an all-stock deal that closed 2 Feb 2026. SpaceX listed on Nasdaq on 12 June 2026. Grok reportedly had 117 million monthly users in March 2026.
players.why: Backed by a public company with launch and satellite revenue, and runs the Colossus clusters.
players.cond: Grok usage and revenue (about $500m annualized, reported) are small against the compute it is buying.

players.stat: 24.4% of text requests on OpenRouter in the week of 21 Sept 2026, ahead of Google and OpenAI (one source).
players.why: Open weights at low prices, popular with developers and in China.
players.cond: Export controls and Chinese compute supply.

players.stat: €3bn Series D at about €21bn, Sept 2026, led by Samsung, Scaleup Europe and PSG Equity (TechCrunch). ASML invested €1.3bn in 2025 for about 11%.
players.why: Sells sovereign AI to European governments and companies.
players.cond: Staying close enough to the frontier to hold customers.

players.stat: Valued at about $32bn with no product revenue. Nvidia planned a $5bn investment in a July 2026 partnership (reported).
players.why: Bets a research breakthrough, not scale alone, wins.
players.cond: Producing a model.

players.stat: Sources conflict: a $12bn seed valuation (July 2025) is the last confirmed. Reports of a $50bn round and of talks at $40bn have not been confirmed.
players.why: Staffed by former OpenAI leaders and backed by a16z.
players.cond: Shipping a product and confirming a round.

players.stat: Last confirmed priced round was a $29.3bn valuation (Nov 2025). SpaceX is reported to be buying it in an all-stock deal worth $60bn. Annualized revenue reported at $3bn by May 2026.
players.why: Owns the coding workflow developers sit in all day.
players.cond: The acquisition status is from a single source, and it depends on models it buys from the labs.

players.stat: About $20bn valuation and about $450m of annualized revenue (Sept 2025). Revenue reported up 50% after moving from ads to subscriptions in February 2026.
players.why: Answer engine that competes with Search without owning a model.
players.cond: No 2026 round confirmed. It buys models from the labs it competes with.

sectors.name: Software
sectors.blurb: The applications companies run on, and the argument over whether agents break the seat-based business.

positions.name: Enterprise applications
positions.metric: 2026 repriced software on the fear that AI agents reduce per-seat demand. Commentators put the February selloff at about $285bn, with one measure of the sector down more than 23% for the year to date. Vendors are moving to usage and per-action pricing.

players.stat: Over 30 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats (July 2026, from 15 million in January). GitHub Copilot at 50 million users, as reported on the call.
players.why: Sells the agents to customers who already pay for its software.
players.cond: Net seat additions are doubling each quarter, which still has to show up as usage.

players.stat: Q2 2026 cloud revenue EUR 6.3bn, up 24% at constant currency. Current cloud backlog EUR 22.9bn, up 27%.
players.why: Runs the finance and supply chain systems that are hardest to replace.
players.cond: It lowered its profit outlook after acquisitions.

players.stat: Q2 2026 subscription revenue $3,877m, up 24.5%. Current remaining performance obligations $13.20bn, up 21%. FY2026 guide $15.76bn to $15.78bn.
players.why: Sits across IT, HR and customer workflows that agents need to act inside.
players.cond: Margins under AI cost pressure.

players.stat: Agentforce ARR passed $1.5bn in Q2 FY27, up more than 240% (reported). It was $800m at the end of FY26.
players.why: Owns the customer data agents work from.
players.cond: Agentic pricing at about $0.10 an action has to replace seat revenue.

players.stat: Fiscal Q2 2027 subscription revenue $2.471bn, up 13.9%. Total subscription backlog up 8%. Silver Lake reportedly in talks to take it private at a valuation above $51bn, with no deal signed.
players.why: Holds HR and payroll data for large employers.
players.cond: Slower backlog growth and whether the private equity talks lead to a deal.

players.stat: Software-as-a-service revenue $4.2bn, up 10%, in the quarter to August 2026.
players.why: Applications run on the same cloud it is building for AI.
players.cond: Growth is far slower than its infrastructure business.

players.stat: Raised $950m at a valuation above $15bn in May 2026. ARR estimates run from $150m to $200m.
players.why: Sells outcomes (resolved customer issues) instead of seats.
players.cond: Competing with Salesforce and ServiceNow, which now sell the same agents.

players.stat: $200m raised in March 2026 at an $11bn valuation.
players.why: A vertical tool built for law firms' work.
players.cond: Frontier labs selling the same capability directly.

players.stat: $250m Series D at a $4.5bn valuation, January 2026.
players.why: Customer support agents sold on resolution rates.
players.cond: Sierra and the incumbents.

players.stat: $300m ARR announced in May 2026. The last priced round was $150m at $7.2bn in June 2025, and later estimates conflict.
players.why: Connects to a company's apps so agents can find and act on its information.
players.cond: Microsoft and Google bundling the same search.

players.stat: $500m Series D at an $11bn valuation, February 2026. A later tender is reported at $22bn.
players.why: Voice is the interface for agents that answer phones.
players.cond: The labs shipping native voice models.

positions.name: Data and analytics
positions.metric: Databricks reported a $7bn revenue run rate in Q2 2026, growing more than 80%, and closed $5bn at a $190bn valuation in August 2026. Snowflake's fiscal Q1 2027 product revenue was $1.334bn, up 34%. Palantir's Q2 2026 revenue was $1.935bn, up 92.8% (reported).

players.stat: $7bn run rate (company), Q2 2026. $5bn raised at $190bn, August 2026, led by Coatue. IPO possible as early as 2027.
players.why: Sells the place where data and models meet, to the same buyers as the cloud.
players.cond: A private valuation this high needs the growth to persist.

players.stat: Fiscal Q1 2027 product revenue $1.334bn, up 34%. FY2026 product revenue $4.47bn.
players.why: Large base of enterprise data warehouses.
players.cond: Databricks growing about twice as fast.

players.stat: Q2 2026 revenue $1.935bn, up 92.8%. FY guide raised to about $8.15bn.
players.why: Sells deployed AI applications to governments and large operators.
players.cond: Valuation, and dependence on a few government buyers.

positions.name: Developer tools and observability
positions.metric: Datadog's Q2 2026 revenue was $1.12bn, up 36%, with 33,400 customers and remaining performance obligations of $3.47bn, up 43%. GitHub Copilot is reported at 50 million users.

players.stat: Q2 2026 revenue $1.12bn, up 36%. Free cash flow $279m. Management attributed its guidance to lower usage from its largest customer (Quartr summary).
players.why: Instruments the applications that AI labs themselves run.
players.cond: Customer concentration in AI-native buyers.

players.stat: Owns Splunk, completed 18 March 2024 for about $28bn.
players.why: Logs and security data from two budgets in one product.
players.cond: Whether a hardware seller can run a software subscription.

players.stat: Reported raising at about $9bn in early 2026, with ARR over $400m. Valuation figures vary from $6bn to $9.5bn.
players.why: Open-source dashboards that customers adopt before they buy.
players.cond: Valuation conflict, and Datadog's pricing power.

sectors.name: Security
sectors.blurb: Who defends the systems, and who is buying the pieces to build one platform.

positions.name: Security platforms
positions.metric: Palo Alto Networks' next-generation security ARR was $9.10bn at the end of fiscal 2026, up 63%, including $1.6bn from CyberArk and Chronosphere. CrowdStrike's ending ARR was about $5.84bn, up 25%. Zscaler's ARR was $3.771bn, up 25%.

players.stat: Fiscal Q4 2026 revenue $3.41bn, up 34%. Next-generation security ARR $9.10bn, up 63%. Targets $20bn by fiscal 2030.
players.why: Bought its way into identity and cloud, so customers consolidate vendors.
players.cond: Part of the growth is acquired, so organic growth is lower than the headline.

players.stat: Q2 fiscal 2027 revenue $1.47bn, up 26%. Record net new ARR of $333m. Falcon Flex accounts exceed $2.29bn of ARR, up 101%.
players.why: One agent and one platform, sold as a flexible credit that customers spend across modules.
players.cond: Microsoft's bundling, and whether net new ARR keeps rising.

players.stat: Q2 2026 revenue $2.05bn, up 26%, and billings $2.37bn, up 33%. 2026 revenue guided to $8.02bn to $8.18bn.
players.why: Sells the firewall and the chip inside it, so it wins on price and performance.
players.cond: A firewall refresh cycle, which may not repeat.

players.stat: Fiscal Q4 2026 ARR $3.771bn, up 25%, or 20% excluding the Red Canary purchase. Revenue $898.2m, up 25%.
players.why: Security delivered from the cloud as companies drop appliances.
players.cond: Organic growth of 20% against bigger platforms.

players.stat: Reported as intensifying competitive pressure on CrowdStrike and others (secondary).
players.why: Bundles security into licences customers already hold.
players.cond: Customers preferring a specialist after a breach.

players.stat: Raised $400m at a $6.4bn valuation, September 2026 (CNBC).
players.why: Makes the browser the control point for security.
players.cond: Displacing the endpoint and network incumbents.

positions.name: Cloud, identity and data security
positions.metric: Google completed its Wiz purchase on 11 March 2026 at a price of about $29.5bn after adjustments (Alphabet 10-Q). Palo Alto Networks closed its roughly $25bn CyberArk purchase on 11 February 2026. Okta's fiscal Q2 2027 revenue was $805m, up 11%.

players.stat: Closed into Google Cloud on 11 Mar 2026 at about $29.5bn. Reported at $1bn of ARR in 2025 (single trade outlet). Products stay available on AWS, Azure and Oracle Cloud.
players.why: The leading cloud security product across all the clouds.
players.cond: Customers on rival clouds trusting a Google-owned tool.

players.stat: Closed into Palo Alto Networks on 11 Feb 2026 at a 26% premium, about $25bn.
players.why: Controls access for privileged human and machine accounts.
players.cond: Integrating it, and agent identity becoming a separate market.

players.stat: Fiscal Q2 2027 revenue $805m, up 11%. New products were about 30% of bookings. Says over 90% of customers run agents in production but only 22% are confident they are controlled (company-reported).
players.why: Pitches identity for AI agents as the next market.
players.cond: Slower growth than the platform vendors, and CyberArk in Palo Alto's hands.

players.stat: Raised $600m at a $12bn valuation in June 2026, led by Evolution Equity Partners. Another source reports a $400m round paired with the Oasis purchase.
players.why: Finds and classifies sensitive data so AI tools do not leak it.
players.cond: Round size conflicts across sources.

players.stat: ServiceNow agreed to pay $7.75bn for Armis.
players.why: Sees every connected device a company owns.
players.cond: Integration into ServiceNow's workflow products.

players.stat: CrowdStrike bought the identity startup for a reported $740m.
players.why: Decides in real time which person or agent gets access.
players.cond: Price is reported, not confirmed.

sectors.name: Internet and consumer platforms
sectors.blurb: Where the money is collected: ads, subscriptions, commerce and games.

positions.name: Search, social and advertising
positions.metric: Google was about 89.9% of global search referral traffic in September 2026 (StatCounter, which measures referrals and not searches). Q2 2026 advertising revenue: Google about $82bn (+14%), Meta $59.36bn (+27%), Amazon $19.8bn (+26%), YouTube $11.1bn (+12.9%) (secondary reports).

players.stat: Roughly $82bn of Q2 2026 advertising revenue, up about 14%. Search near 90% of referral traffic. AI Mode in Search passed 1 billion monthly users.
players.why: Owns the queries, the browser and the phone's default.
players.cond: Chat assistants taking questions, though AI-native engines were reported under 0.1% each (single source).

players.stat: Q2 2026 ad revenue $59.36bn, up 27%, on 3.60 billion daily people. Impressions up 14% and price per ad up 12%.
players.why: Grows ad revenue far faster than its audience by showing better matches.
players.cond: Capital spending of $130bn to $145bn and soft third-quarter guidance.

players.stat: Advertising services $19.8bn in Q2 2026, up 26%.
players.why: Ads placed where people are already shopping.
players.cond: Whether AI shopping assistants route buyers around its pages.

players.stat: US joint venture closed 22 January 2026. Oracle, Silver Lake and MGX hold 15% each, existing ByteDance investors 30.1% and ByteDance 19.9%. US daily users held at about 95% of earlier levels (Sensor Tower).
players.why: Kept its US users through the ownership change.
players.cond: Whether the recommendation algorithm stays as strong under the new owners.

players.stat: ChatGPT is the main consumer alternative to search. AI-native engines were reported under 0.1% of search referrals each (single source, unverified).
players.why: Many questions now start in a chat window.
players.cond: Measurement is unsettled, and no ad business at scale is verified.

positions.name: Video and streaming
positions.metric: Nielsen's Gauge for July 2026: streaming was 49.0% of US TV time, with YouTube at a record 14.2%, Disney's streaming services 4.7% combined and Peacock 2.6%. In June, Netflix was 7.9% and Prime Video 4.2%.

players.stat: YouTube at 14.2% of TV time in July 2026, the largest single service.
players.why: Free, enormous catalogue, and creators supply the content.
players.cond: Brand-safety and creator payments.

players.stat: Q3 2026 revenue $12.87bn, up 12%. Operating margin 34.6%. 2026 ad revenue target cut to $2.7bn from about $3bn. About 1,000 jobs, or 6%, being cut.
players.why: Highest margins among the video services.
players.cond: Its share of TV time slipped to 7.9% in June, and its ad business is slower than planned.

players.stat: Prime Video at 4.2% of TV time in June 2026.
players.why: Bundled with shipping.
players.cond: Ad load and sports rights.

players.stat: 4.7% of TV time for its combined streaming services in July 2026.
players.why: Studios and parks feed the service.
players.cond: Combined figure is not Disney+ alone.

players.stat: Warner Bros. Discovery merger signed 27 Feb 2026 at $31 a share in cash. It closed on 6 October 2026 after a state attorneys general suit.
players.why: Combines two studios and two streaming services for scale.
players.cond: Integration and debt.

positions.name: Commerce platforms
positions.metric: Shopify's gross merchandise volume was $115.6bn in Q2 2026, up 32%, on revenue of $3.6bn, up 34% (10-Q). Amazon's net sales were $200.6bn, up 20%.

players.stat: Q2 2026 net sales $200.6bn, up 20%. AWS $42.2bn.
players.why: Logistics, Prime and ads reinforce one another.
players.cond: Agents shopping across sites.

players.stat: GMV $115.6bn in Q2 2026, up 32%. Revenue $3.6bn, up 34%. AI-attributed traffic and orders each tripled, though management says the channel is still small.
players.why: Powers the merchants that compete with Amazon, and is building catalogue tools for AI agents.
players.cond: AI agents choosing among stores.

positions.name: Games
positions.metric: Tencent's domestic games revenue was RMB 47.3bn in Q2 2026, up 17%, and international games RMB 18.6bn, down 0.8%. Roblox bookings grew 8% to about $1.6bn with 123 million daily users.

players.stat: Total revenue RMB 204.8bn in Q2 2026, up 11%. Free cash flow turned negative as AI capital spending rose.
players.why: Owns the distribution through WeChat and the studios.
players.cond: AI spending and flat overseas games.

players.stat: Q2 2026 bookings up 8% to about $1.6bn. Daily users 123 million, down from a 152 million peak in Q3 2025. Q3 outlook is for negative bookings growth.
players.why: User-built worlds give it content it does not pay for.
players.cond: Spend per hour fell among younger US and Canadian users.

sectors.name: Devices
sectors.blurb: The phones, laptops and glasses people carry, all squeezed by the same memory shortage.

positions.name: Smartphones
positions.metric: Q2 2026 shipments of 276.3 million, down 7.4% (IDC). Samsung 62.7m and 22.7% share, Apple 55.7m and 20.2%, Xiaomi about 11.3%, OPPO 10.4%, vivo 7.6%. IDC expects 2026 shipments to fall 16.7% to just over 1bn, the steepest annual drop on record.

players.stat: 62.7m units and 22.7% share in Q2 2026, up about 8%.
players.why: Sells across every price band and makes its own memory.
players.cond: Memory costs are raising phone prices (IDC: average price up 27.6%).

players.stat: 55.7m units and 20.2% share in Q2 2026, up about 15%. Samsung and Apple were the only top-five vendors that grew.
players.why: Premium buyers keep buying as prices rise.
players.cond: Component costs.

players.stat: About 11.2% to 11.3% share, with the steepest decline among the top vendors (down 26.3% in one IDC-based table).
players.why: Value-priced phones are hit hardest by memory prices.
players.cond: Sources differ on its exact share.

players.stat: 10.4% share, down 17.5% (IDC-based table).
players.why: Large presence in Asia.
players.cond: Memory costs.

players.stat: 7.6% share, down 19.4% (IDC-based table).
players.why: Large presence in Asia.
players.cond: Memory costs.

positions.name: PCs
positions.metric: Q2 2026 PC shipments of 68.2 million, down 4.9% (IDC). Lenovo 24.4%, HP 19.1%, Dell 13.6% and Apple 9.9%. Counterpoint puts the decline at 4%, and IDC expects the DRAM shortage to last into early 2028.

players.stat: 24.4% share, shipments down 2.1% (IDC).
players.why: Scale and a wide range.
players.cond: Memory costs.

players.stat: 19.1% share, shipments down 9% (IDC).
players.why: Commercial and consumer base.
players.cond: Memory costs.

players.stat: 13.6% share, shipments down 5% (IDC).
players.why: Enterprise customers.
players.cond: Server business is now the bigger growth story.

players.stat: 6.7 million Macs and 9.9% share in Q2 2026, up about 10% (IDC), the only major maker to grow. IDC credits the MacBook Neo launch in part.
players.why: Rising while the rest of the market falls.
players.cond: Whether the new low-price Mac holds its volume as memory costs rise.

positions.name: Smart glasses and XR
positions.metric: XR and smart glasses shipments grew about 35% in Q2 2026 (IDC), down from 130% in the prior quarter. Glasses are nearly 85% of XR shipments and headsets about 15%. Meta's share of smart glasses is put at 69% to 76% depending on the source.

players.stat: Share of smart glasses reported at 69.2% in Q1 2026 and 76.1% in another IDC citation. Ray-Ban Display's international rollout was paused because US availability was backlogged. A $299 display-free line launched 23 June 2026.
players.why: Sells glasses through eyewear stores, not as a headset.
players.cond: Display glasses are supply constrained.

players.stat: Sold over 7 million Ray-Ban and Oakley Meta glasses in 2025. First-half 2026 revenue from Meta glasses nearly doubled.
players.why: Makes the frames and owns the retail.
players.cond: Depends on one platform partner.

players.stat: Google and Samsung plan Android XR glasses, starting with an audio-led model in fall 2026. No confirmed launch date or price.
players.why: Brings an operating system and Gemini to the category.
players.cond: Shipping a product people buy.

sectors.name: Telecom and connectivity
sectors.blurb: The carriers, the equipment makers, the satellites and the networks that carry everything else.

positions.name: US carriers
positions.metric: AT&T's Q3 2026: 379,000 postpaid phone net adds at 0.92% churn, 442,000 fiber net adds and 327,000 fixed wireless adds. Debt of $159.6bn. Verizon guided to the upper half of 750,000 to 1 million postpaid phone net adds for 2026.

players.stat: Q3 2026: 379,000 postpaid phone net adds, churn 0.92%, 442,000 fiber adds. Plans over 60 million fiber locations by 2030.
players.why: Sells wireless and fiber together.
players.cond: Total debt of $159.6bn, which it attributes partly to spectrum purchases.

players.stat: Raised 2026 guidance twice. First positive first-quarter postpaid phone net adds since 2013. Q3 results due 26 October 2026.
players.why: Turnaround after years of subscriber losses.
players.cond: Q3 results had not been reported when this was compiled.

players.stat: No 2026 results were verified in this research. A report says Deutsche Telekom is weighing a full takeover (unverified).
players.why: Largest 5G network by coverage claims.
players.cond: Figures not checked here.

positions.name: Mobile network equipment
positions.metric: Dell'Oro's 1H26 ranking: Huawei, Ericsson, Nokia, ZTE and Samsung hold 96% of the RAN market. Huawei and Ericsson together held nearly two-thirds in late 2025. The market was flat in 2Q 2026, with Huawei strong and Ericsson softer than expected.

players.stat: Number one globally by RAN revenue and gained share outside China (Dell'Oro).
players.why: Competitive on price and technology where it is allowed to sell.
players.cond: Western restrictions.

players.stat: Clear number two. Q2 2026 performance softer than expected (Dell'Oro).
players.why: Largest Western supplier.
players.cond: Huawei's share gains.

players.stat: Third in 1H26. Lost ground between 2019 and 2025 (Dell'Oro).
players.why: Western alternative with a broad portfolio.
players.cond: Winning share with AI-focused radio products.

players.stat: Fourth in 1H26 (Dell'Oro).
players.why: Chinese domestic demand.
players.cond: Western restrictions.

players.stat: Fifth in 1H26 (Dell'Oro).
players.why: Sells mainly in the US, Japan and Korea.
players.cond: Small share against the top two.

positions.name: Satellite connectivity
positions.metric: Starlink reached 13.6 million subscribers in Q3 2026, up from 12 million in Q2 and 10.3 million in Q1, with average revenue of $69 a user. Connectivity revenue was $5.25bn in the quarter.

players.stat: 13.6 million subscribers across 174 markets, with 1.6 million added in Q3 2026. SpaceX's total revenue was $14.6bn in the quarter, up 161%, with AI the largest business at $7.56bn (reported).
players.why: Launches its own satellites at a cost no rival matches.
players.cond: SpaceX counts service lines, so a household with two plans counts twice.

positions.name: Network edge and delivery
positions.metric: Cloudflare's Q2 2026 revenue was $696.1m, up 36%, with 4,698 customers above $100,000 a year, up 27%. Gross margin fell 3.2 points to 73.1% on higher network costs.

players.stat: Revenue $696.1m, up 36%. Non-GAAP operating income $96.1m. Raised full-year guidance.
players.why: Sells security and delivery from one global network, and is building for AI agents.
players.cond: Gross margin down as paid traffic grows.

players.stat: No 2026 figure was verified in this research.
players.why: Long-standing delivery and security customer base.
players.cond: Unchecked.

sectors.name: Foundation
sectors.blurb: The packaging, wafers and magnets that sit under every chip and motor.

positions.name: Advanced packaging and substrates
positions.metric: TSMC's CoWoS capacity is estimated to reach 115,000 to 140,000 wafers a month by the end of 2026, and TSMC does not disclose it. Nvidia is estimated at about 60% of capacity and Nvidia, Broadcom and AMD together at 85% or more. TrendForce reports the supply gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by the end of 2026. Three companies make about 75% of ABF substrates.

players.stat: Ramping CoWoS packaging from about 75,000 to 80,000 wafers a month toward 120,000 to 130,000 by the end of 2026 (estimates).
players.why: Packages the chips it makes, so the customer buys the whole stack from one place.
players.cond: Capacity expansion. TrendForce expects the squeeze to ease from 2027.

players.stat: Unimicron, Ibiden and Shinko control about 75% of the ABF substrate market. New lines take 18 to 24 months.
players.why: Few companies can make the substrates, and adding capacity is slow.
players.cond: No shortage-specific capacity data was found.

players.stat: Q1 2026 revenue NT$173.7bn, up 17%. Its assembly, test and materials unit grew nearly 30%. CoWoS-type output is projected at 20,000 to 25,000 wafers a month by year end (brokerage estimate).
players.why: Takes the overflow when TSMC's own lines are full.
players.cond: Whether it wins the flagship customers' volume.

players.stat: Record Q1 2026 revenue of $1.68bn, up 27%. 2026 capital spending $2.5bn to $3bn. A 10-year CoWoS agreement with TSMC (June 2026) and a $1.5bn advanced-packaging deal with Nvidia (July) are reported by one commentary source.
players.why: Gives US customers a US packaging option, with an Arizona campus.
players.cond: The two agreements are single-sourced.

positions.name: Silicon wafers
positions.metric: Shin-Etsu and SUMCO together hold over 50% of 300mm wafer supply (Future Market Insights, a secondary estimate). No 2026 SEMI shipment data and no GlobalWafers share was found.

players.stat: Over 50% of global 300mm supply between them. SUMCO plans to end 200mm production at Miyazaki by late 2026 to focus on 300mm AI-grade wafers.
players.why: Wafer making is a slow, specialist craft that the chip makers buy from two suppliers.
players.cond: Share is a secondary estimate, and the data here is thin.

positions.name: Rare earths and magnets
positions.metric: China's April 2025 export licensing for seven medium and heavy rare earths remains in force. A second wave of controls is suspended until 10 November 2026. China's rare earth and magnet exports in January and February 2026 were under one third of the same months in 2024 and 2025. A US defense procurement ban on Chinese magnets takes full effect on 1 January 2027.

players.stat: Controls licensing for exports of rare earths and the magnets that contain them. Beijing had not ruled out the most expansive version of its controls as of May 2026.
players.why: Processes most of the world's rare earths, so a licence decides who builds motors.
players.cond: The suspension of the second wave expires on 10 November 2026.

players.stat: Q2 2026 NdPr production 840 tonnes, up 41%. Revenue $108.5m, up 89%. Magnetics revenue $16.5m, with capital spending of $230.3m, over 60% on magnets. Signed an offtake for separated gadolinium with a US aerospace and defense customer.
players.why: The only scaled US producer, with price protection income that supports it.
players.cond: US magnet capacity is not expected to be meaningful until 2028 (one source).

sectors.name: Fintech and payments
sectors.blurb: Who moves the money, who is replacing the bank account and who issues the digital dollar.

positions.name: Payments
positions.metric: Visa's payments volume passed $4tn in a quarter for the first time in fiscal Q3 2026, up 10% at constant dollars, with net revenue of $11.6bn, up 14%. Mastercard's Q2 2026 gross dollar volume was $2.9tn, up 8%, with cross-border up 12%. Stripe processed $1.9tn in 2025, up 34%.

players.stat: Fiscal Q3 2026 net revenue $11.6bn, up 14%. Value-added services $3.8bn, up 34%. Processed transactions 71.7bn.
players.why: Every card payment on its network pays it a fee, and it sells extra services on top.
players.cond: Stablecoins and account-to-account payments routing around cards.

players.stat: Q2 2026 net revenue $9.3bn, up 14%. Gross dollar volume $2.9tn, up 8%. Value-added services up 20%.
players.why: Same network economics, with strength in cross-border.
players.cond: The same threat from payments that bypass cards.

players.stat: $1.9tn processed in 2025, up 34%. Valued at $159bn in a February 2026 employee tender. Reported to have joined Advent in a $53.4bn proposal for PayPal.
players.why: The default way online businesses accept payments.
players.cond: The PayPal proposal is unconfirmed, and no board response was found.

players.stat: Q1 2026 payment volume $464bn, up 11%. A reported $60.50 a share proposal from Stripe and Advent, about 28% above the prior close, with equity of $17bn including Block and about $50bn of bank financing.
players.why: Large user base and brand at a valuation that attracted a bid.
players.cond: Whether its board engages, and whether the deal is real.

players.stat: Q1 2026 processed volume EUR 382bn, up 21%. Net revenue up 16%, or 20% at constant currency.
players.why: Sells one platform to large global merchants.
players.cond: Stripe moving upmarket.

players.stat: Named in the reported PayPal proposal as an equity partner. Market value about $37bn in one undated comparison.
players.why: Owns both the merchant terminal and the consumer app.
players.cond: No 2026 volume figure was found.

positions.name: Digital banks and lenders
positions.metric: Customer counts are not comparable. Nubank reports about 139 million customers (secondary). Revolut cites 68 to 80 million. Chime counts 10.4 million active members, up 20%. Public markets value listed neobanks at about 4 to 5 times revenue, against Revolut's private price near 19 times (secondary estimate).

players.stat: About 139 million customers and $1.1bn of net income in Q2 2026 (secondary).
players.why: Won a large banking market with a cheap digital model.
players.cond: Unaudited figures from trackers.

players.stat: Reported valuation of $115bn in July 2026 from an employee share sale. Customers reported at 68 to 80 million.
players.why: Sells a broad bundle of accounts, trading and travel in one app.
players.cond: Private valuation near 19 times revenue.

players.stat: Q2 2026 revenue $670m, up 27%. Active members 10.4 million, up 20%. Stock near $33 against a $27 IPO price.
players.why: Public and growing in the largest consumer banking market.
players.cond: Counts active members, not registered customers.

players.stat: 15.8 million members and about 24.4 million products by Q2 2026 in one source, and 14.7 million members in another.
players.why: Cross-sells loans, banking and investing to its members.
players.cond: Member counts conflict.

positions.name: Stablecoins and crypto

sectors.name: Mobility and autonomy
sectors.blurb: Who is putting cars on the road without drivers, and who is selling the electric ones.

positions.name: Robotaxis

Waymo is reported at about 500,000 paid rides a week after a $16bn round at a $126bn valuation in February 2026. Sources disagree on fleet and city counts.

players.stat: Robotaxi in seven metros in the first half of 2026 with 44 active vehicles (one source). Cybercab rides began in Austin on 3 September. Unsupervised miles rose about eightfold in the quarter, and Dallas is next (call summary). Revenue is not expected until Q2 2027.
players.why: Already builds millions of cars with the sensors and software to carry the service.
players.cond: Timelines slipped in its Q3 call, and the fleet figures are older and secondary.

players.why: Designed the vehicle with no driver's seat.
players.cond: Small fleet.

players.stat: Q2 2026 revenue $36.2m, up about 69%, with robotaxi revenue $12.1m. Fleet 1,975 on 30 June, targeting over 3,500 by year end. Uber is contracted for more than 2,000 robotaxis in Europe.
players.why: Public company with a growing fleet and a global distribution deal.
players.cond: Revenue is small against its fleet.

players.stat: About 3,400 level-4 vehicles in the first half of 2026, more than 1,800 of them robotaxis.
players.why: Runs robotaxis across several countries.
players.cond: Single source.

players.stat: Record commercial driverless miles in Q1 2026 with FedEx, Hirschbach, Werner and Uber Freight. FY26 revenue guidance $14m to $16m reaffirmed.
players.why: Applies driverless technology to long-haul freight.
players.cond: No Q2 2026 figures were found.

positions.name: Electric vehicles
positions.metric: Q3 2026: BYD sold 762,478 passenger battery electric vehicles, up 30.9%, against Tesla's 486,532 deliveries, down 2%. Global EV sales were 15.5 million in the first nine months of 2026. China's domestic EV sales fell 18% in September while Europe rose 39%.

players.stat: 762,478 passenger battery electric vehicles in Q3 2026, up 30.9% (third-party sales charts, not a filing). 87.7 GWh of EV batteries installed in H1 2026.
players.why: Makes its own batteries and sells in China, Europe and emerging markets.
players.cond: China's domestic market fell 18% in September.

players.stat: Q3 2026 deliveries 486,532, down 2% from 497,099 a year earlier, beating a consensus of about 462,000.
players.why: Sells vehicles, software and energy storage from one company.
players.cond: BYD's battery electric lead was 275,946 vehicles.

sectors.name: Robotics
sectors.blurb: The factory robots that already work, and the humanoids and robot models still arriving.

positions.name: Industrial and warehouse robots
positions.metric: The IFR counted 603,000 industrial robots installed worldwide in 2025, up 11%, and a global stock of 5 million. China installed 354,000, or 59%. The US passed Japan to become the second-largest market with about 38,500 units, up 12%. Amazon runs more than 1 million warehouse robots, a figure last announced in July 2025.

players.stat: Domestic suppliers held about 55% of China's market in 2025, down from 57% (one source). China installed 354,000 robots.
players.why: Their home market is more than half of the world, and buyers there prefer local suppliers.
players.cond: Sources differ on growth rates for China's installs, from 15% to 20%.

players.stat: More than 1 million warehouse robots, announced on 1 July 2025 and not updated since. It also employs more than 1.5 million people.
players.why: Runs the largest fleet of robots in one company.
players.cond: The count is a floor and a year old.

positions.name: Humanoid robots
positions.metric: Chinese makers accounted for over 97% of about 19,100 humanoids shipped globally in H1 2026 (one report, roughly triple the prior year's first half). Tesla's Optimus output is reported far below its target. Counts of units deployed are secondary and conflict.

players.stat: Unitree, UBTech and AgiBot shipped most of about 19,100 humanoids in H1 2026. One report says Unitree is pursuing a $6.2bn IPO, which was not confirmed.
players.why: Scale manufacturing and low prices at home.
players.cond: Single-source shipment count.

players.stat: Reports conflict between over 1,000 Optimus Gen 3 units in its own factories and a few hundred against a 5,000 target. Management's target is 20,000 a week within about a year, with deliveries not before late 2027 by one account.
players.why: Could use its own factories and vehicle supply chain.
players.cond: Timelines keep moving.

players.stat: Reported to have deployed 40 Figure 03 units at BMW's Spartanburg plant in January 2026, billed at about $25 per robot-hour. A recent $1bn raise is mentioned without a confirmed valuation.
players.why: Has the strongest commercial deployment evidence among US startups.
players.cond: Single-source figures.

players.stat: About 250 Digit units in logistics (market tracker).
players.why: Built for a narrow warehouse task.
players.cond: No funding figure was verified.

players.stat: About 80 Apollo units deployed (market tracker).
players.why: Partnered with industrial customers.
players.cond: No funding figure was verified.

players.stat: Over 10,000 pre-orders for the NEO home robot, with deliveries expected by the end of 2026 (one source).
players.why: Aims at the home and not the factory.
players.cond: Single source, and no funding figure was verified.

positions.name: Robot foundation models
positions.metric: No starter was verified in this row. Skild AI raised close to $1.4bn led by SoftBank, with Nvidia's venture arm participating, at a valuation above $14bn in January 2026. Physical Intelligence was last reported at $5.6bn in November 2025.

players.why: Builds one model that controls many kinds of robots.
players.cond: A later round and an acquisition of a Zebra division are reported in single sources.

players.why: Works on a general-purpose model that robots from different makers can use.
players.cond: Round status unconfirmed.

sectors.name: Health technology
sectors.blurb: The AI tools doctors use, the drugs AI claims to have found, and the robots in the operating room.

positions.name: Clinical AI
positions.metric: No usage share exists for AI scribes. Abridge reports over $100m of ARR and more than 300 health systems, including all 40 Kaiser Permanente hospitals. OpenEvidence is reported at $15bn after a $250m round in September 2026 with about $300m of annualized revenue. Valuations come from aggregators.

players.stat: $5.3bn valuation, over $100m of ARR, more than 300 health systems. Integrated with Epic.
players.why: Won the largest health systems early and plugs into the main medical record.
players.cond: Epic and Microsoft's Dragon Copilot were not researched here, and both sell similar tools.

players.stat: Reported $243m Series C and a valuation above $1bn.
players.why: Sells scribe and coding together.
players.cond: Smaller than Abridge.

players.stat: $126m raised in November 2025 at a $3.5bn valuation, about $404m in total.
players.why: Sells agents that call patients and handle routine staff tasks.
players.cond: No 2026 round was found.

players.why: Clinicians use it to look things up, and advertising can pay for it.
players.cond: Earlier valuations come from sources that do not fully agree.

positions.name: AI drug discovery
positions.metric: No drug discovered mainly by AI has been approved yet, and AI-designed drugs fail in Phase 2 about as often as other drugs (one source). Insilico's rentosertib is the most advanced AI-linked candidate, in a 320-patient Phase 3 trial whose start date is reported as July or September 2026.

players.stat: Rentosertib for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in a registered 320-patient Phase 3, with sources conflicting on timing.
players.why: First with both an AI-found target and an AI-designed molecule at this stage.
players.cond: Trial results, which are years away.

players.stat: Lead program REC-4881 is listed as Phase 2 in one source and Phase 1b/2 in another.
players.why: Runs its own automated labs to feed models.
players.cond: Stage is unclear across sources.

players.stat: $2.1bn Series B announced 12 May 2026. First clinical trials expected by the end of 2026. No molecule disclosed as of May.
players.why: Built on the protein-structure research that won a Nobel Prize.
players.cond: One source's claim of $3bn in pharma partnerships is uncorroborated.

players.stat: First drug programs reportedly revealed in October 2026, preclinical.
players.why: Large funding to build models and a lab at once.
players.cond: Single source.

positions.name: Surgical robots
positions.metric: Intuitive's da Vinci installed base was about 11,710 systems at 30 June 2026, up 12%. Da Vinci procedures grew about 15% and Ion procedures about 36% in Q2. US da Vinci growth slowed to 12%, which management tied to the expiry of enhanced ACA subsidies.

players.stat: 468 da Vinci systems placed in Q2 2026, 246 of them da Vinci 5. 2026 da Vinci procedure growth guided to 13.5% to 15.5%. Shares fell about 12% on the guidance.
players.why: An installed base of nearly 12,000 robots that surgeons are trained on.
players.cond: US procedure growth slowing from 14% to 12%.

sectors.name: Defense and space
sectors.blurb: The rockets that reach orbit, the startups taking defense work and the primes with the backlogs.

positions.name: Launch
positions.metric: Since early March 2026 the only US heavy rocket able to fly several national security missions has been SpaceX's Falcon 9. ULA's Vulcan last flew on 12 February and has been paused since. Blue Origin's New Glenn exploded during a static-fire test on 28 May and had not returned to flight as of the latest report. No 2026 SpaceX launch count was found.

players.stat: Falcon 9 is the only vehicle flying the missions Vulcan paused. Starship's 2026 flight history conflicts across sources.
players.why: The only operator with a rocket that flies often and reuses its boosters.
players.cond: Starship has to reach orbit reliably and carry payloads.

players.stat: New Glenn's third flight on 19 April left AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 in the wrong orbit. It exploded in a static-fire test on 28 May.
players.why: Backed by deep funding and an Amazon Leo contract.
players.cond: Return to flight.

players.stat: Vulcan's last flight, USSF-87 on 12 February, reached its orbits despite a solid rocket motor anomaly. No launches since.
players.why: Holds long-standing national security contracts.
players.cond: Return to flight.

players.stat: The Neutron rocket's debut reportedly slipped into 2027 after a dome technical issue (one source). No Q2 2026 results were found.
players.why: A mid-size rocket would fill the gap between small launchers and heavy ones.
players.cond: Date is single-sourced.

positions.name: Defense technology
positions.metric: Anduril raised $5bn in a Series H at a $61bn valuation in May 2026, more than double its valuation a year earlier, and reported $2.2bn of 2025 revenue. A round near $100bn was reported in talks in July, unconfirmed.

players.why: Builds weapons and autonomous systems as products and sells them to the Pentagon.

players.stat: Q2 2026 revenue $1.935bn, up 92.8%. Its defense mix was not researched here.
players.why: Sells deployed software to governments.

positions.name: Defense primes

Lockheed's backlog was $230.4bn at 28 June, up from $193.6bn at the end of 2025. The House advanced a $1.15tn FY2027 defense bill (reported), and the 2027 defense authorization had not been enacted.

players.stat: Q2 2026 revenue $24.71bn, up 14%. Sales guidance raised to $95bn to $96bn.
players.why: Sells engines and defense systems to commercial and military buyers.
players.cond: Defense budgets and authorization timing.

players.stat: Adjusted EPS of $7.94 in Q2 2026. 2026 revenue guide $79.75bn to $81.75bn.
players.why: Prime on the largest fighter, missile and space programs.
players.cond: If the authorization act is not signed by 1 October, multiyear procurement contracts cannot go out.

sectors.name: Quantum computing
sectors.blurb: Who is racing to build a fault-tolerant machine, and which listed companies are living on revenue meanwhile.

positions.name: The fault-tolerance race
positions.metric: IBM's roadmap lists a 2026 target of circuits of 7,500 gates across up to three 120-qubit Nighthawk modules, and a fault-tolerant machine, Starling, with 200 logical qubits running 100 million gates in 2029. Quantinuum's Helios is a 98-qubit trapped-ion system launched in November 2025. No independent benchmark ranks the leaders.

players.stat: Roadmap: Nighthawk in 2026 and Starling, 200 logical qubits and 100 million gates, in 2029 (IBM roadmap).
players.why: Publishes dates for each step and the engineering to meet them.
players.cond: A reported 2026 advantage claim was later reproduced classically in at least one case (third-party tracker).

players.stat: Willow was the first processor to operate below the error-correction threshold. No 2026 roadmap update was found.
players.why: Showed errors falling as the machine grew.
players.cond: That result does not yet show fault tolerance at a useful scale.

players.stat: Nasdaq IPO on 4 June 2026 at $60 a share raising about $1.68bn. Valuation reports range from about $13bn to $15bn, with higher figures before pricing. Honeywell is its backer.
players.why: Trapped-ion machines with high accuracy, and the cash to scale.
players.cond: Valuation sources conflict.

players.stat: No 2026 valuation or funding was found. Reported to be breaking ground on large compute centers in Chicago and Brisbane in 2026.
players.why: Bets on photonics and building big facilities first.
players.cond: Funding and status unverified.

positions.name: Listed quantum companies

players.why: Grew revenue fast by buying other companies.
players.cond: Dilution from the equity offering and acquisitions.

players.stat: Q2 revenue $5.1m against $1.8m a year earlier. About $541m of cash and no debt.
players.why: Large cash cushion.

players.stat: Q2 revenue $3.1m, flat. Bookings $2.1m, up 59%. First-half bookings $35.5m include a $20m system sale.
players.why: Sells annealing systems to customers now.

players.why: The first European quantum hardware company on a major US exchange.
players.cond: Listing details need a filing to confirm.

players.why: Neutral-atom approach, an alternative to ions and superconducting circuits.

players.cond: Section 232 tariff decisions, which could delay customers' bookings.
